newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu aide wants Israel to rethink PLO talks.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu aide wants Israel to rethink PLO talks.

text.p: A top aide to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Monday Israel must consider carefully before resuming peace talks with the PLO because of the killing of three Arab land dealers in the West Bank in one month.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's Authority denied allegations by Israeli police that PLO officials were involved in the slayings but Israeli leaders said evidence pointed to Arafat's security agencies.

"These things don't square with the will for peace. They don't square with talk of democracy," said Netanyahu's media adviser David Bar-Illan a day after police said they had "solid evidence" PLO security officials were involved in the killings.
"They don't square with negotiations and we must consider carefully if we should continue talks with people who represent such fascist theories," he told Israel's army radio.

Netanyahu, who convened top cabinet ministers and security officials to discuss the killings, decided to send the Authority a "harsh protest" over the killings and issue arrest warrants against Palestinian suspects.

Three Arab land dealers have been slain in the West Bank since Palestinian Justice Minister Freih Abu Medeen said last month Arabs who sold land to Jews could face the death penalty if convicted in court.

The ban was imposed weeks after the ground breaking of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem which brought peace efforts to a halt. Palestinians say such building pre-empts final status talks on Arab land occupied by Israel in 1967. Those talks have yet to begin under Netanyahu.
Israeli police arrested six Palestinians on Saturday suspected of abducting a land dealer and later said four of the six worked for a branch of Palestinian security.
"There is no directive by Chairman Arafat or the Palestinian Authority to execute people. There is a directive to pursue them legally and in the courts," said Arafat's aide Ahmed Tibi.
Israel's Haaretz newspaper said on Monday Arafat's self-rule Authority had prepared a hit list of 16 Arab land dealers and ordered them killed.

"The list was prepared by the Palestinian Authority and handed to the various (Palestinian) security agencies," the newspaper said, quoting an Israeli security source involved in the investigation of the killings.
Netanyahu said in a radio interview Israel could not conduct "business as usual" with the Palestinian Authority while Arab land dealers were being killed.
"Israeli police are conducting an investigation which points in the direction of senior (Palestinian) officials," Netanyahu told army radio.
Israeli officials had consistently said they suspected the Palestinian administration was involved in the killings but PLO officials deny it.
The man kidnapped on Saturday was known to have co-operated with 34-year-old Ali Mohammad Jumhour, the latest land dealer to be killed in the West Bank, an Israeli police spokeswoman said.
She said a Palestinian intelligence branch, which she did not name, bore responsibility for the killing of Jumhour and Farid Bashiti, the first dealer killed.
In Gaza, Israeli soldiers beat five Palestinians on Monday during scuffles over an Israeli attempt to fence off Arab-owned land in a part of Gaza under Israeli occupation, witnesses said.
